subject: Voyager: feature gating & sprint commitment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Emma Chen <emma.chen@voyager.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Voyager: feature gating & sprint commitment

Team — forwarding final asks from Voyager (attached SOW + req matrix). Short version: they will sign if we can commit to two discrete deliverables before their go-live window. They want: 

1) Tenant pinning & deterministic model affinity (so their traffic is routed to a reserved pool) — must be live for canary by May 15.
2) Telemetry export (per-tenant latency & token-level cost breakdown) delivered to a secure S3 location + proof of retention settings by May 22.

Voyager's legal/procurement are waiting for an engineering commitment to include in the SOW; sales is offering a 12-month reserved commitment if we meet the dates. Key constraints we discussed with the customer: 5k qps peak, 99.9% p50 latency target under current model mix, and data residency in us-east-1.

Can product/eng give a sprint-level commitment? From a timing perspective, we need a green light (yes/no) by EOD Monday so Monica can lock the contract signature cadence. If we can't meet both dates, they asked for a split delivery plan (pinning first, telemetry as follow-on).

Attachments: Voyager_SOW_v2.docx, voyager_requirements_matrix.xlsx (both attached to this thread).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Accounts 
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voyager: feature gating & sprint commitment

Vanessa — thanks for the clear ask and the docs. Quick read and engineering take:

- Tenant pinning / model affinity: this is a moderate-scope change (routing + placement + small serving runtime flags). We estimate ~2.5 engineer-weeks to implement a minimally-viable path that supports per-tenant pinning to a dedicated pool and a canary. That assumes existing affinity plumbing (ENG-4521) is merged — otherwise add ~3 days.

- Telemetry export: building the export pipeline (token-level cost + per-request latency + retention controls) and secure S3 delivery with IAM policies is larger — estimate ~3.5–4 engineer-weeks if we do it end-to-end with QA and docs. We can break it down: basic telemetry + redaction + S3 delivery in Sprint A, retention controls and onboarding docs in Sprint B.

Questions for Voyager (please confirm so we can firm estimates):
- Peak qps confirmation (5k) — is that sustained or burst?
- Do they require encryption-at-rest beyond standard S3-KMS?
- Any rollout constraints (canary only to 10% of traffic at first)?

I linked ENG-4521 which is relevant for placement routing. If we can prioritize pinning as a targeted story in Sprint 24 (starts May 6), we can aim for a canary by May 15. Telemetry realistically lands late in Sprint 25 (target May 27–29).

Irene Choi
Director, Product Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@voyager.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voyager: feature gating & sprint commitment

Thanks Vanessa — clarifications below so the team can firm up the plan: 

- Peak: 5k qps is a peak sustained during daytime hours in week 1 of rollout; expected steady state ~1.2k qps.
- Latency SLO: we're asking for p50 < 120ms and p95 < 400ms for tenant traffic under the reserve pool. We will accept a staged approach: canary at 5% traffic first.
- Security: S3 with KMS is sufficient, but we need proof of the bucket's lifecycle policy (30 day raw retention, 12 month aggregated retention) and an audit log (who accessed it).
- Acceptance criteria: 1) pinning works for 5% canary, 2) telemetry file schema validated and delivered to our S3 bucket, 3) brief runbook for rollback.

Procurement note: we'll need dates in the SOW and a commitment to the canary window before signing.

Emma Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Voyager Inc.
emma.chen@voyager.com
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Chen <emma.chen@voyager.com>, procurement@voyager.com
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Voyager: feature gating & sprint commitment

Irene — thanks for the rapid estimates, and Emma — thanks for the clarifications. Pragmatic ask from sales: can we lock pinning into Sprint 24 (start May 6) as a committed story (MV pinning + 5% canary + rollback runbook)? Can telemetry (schema + S3 delivery) be scoped as a separate committed story in Sprint 25 with a targeted delivery window May 27–29?

If engineering agrees to the above split, Voyager will sign the SOW and we will convert the opportunity to a reserved capacity contract (12 months) — this materially improves the economics. 

If we need more runway, please propose the minimal gating changes that let us ship a canary (even if it's feature-flagged and limited). We need a firm yes/no by COB Monday (Apr 22) so I can close procurement timelines.

Next steps: 
- Irene / Priyom: confirm Sprint 24 pinning commitment or propose exact scope reduction by Monday COB.
- Ben: if we commit, please coordinate a high-level QA plan and any performance testing window.
- Vanessa: I will update the SOW dates once we have a commitment.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
